# spec/xml/reader

`spec/xml/reader` — a narrow XML reader for RFC XML v3 (RFC 7991), as
xml2rfc and kramdown-rfc write it. No dependency and no network: this
tokenizer is the whole reader.

The document is untrusted input, so the reader is narrow on purpose:

  - A DOCTYPE may carry no SYSTEM or PUBLIC identifier, and its internal
    subset may hold nothing but general entities whose value is one numeric
    character reference (`<!ENTITY nbsp "&#160;">`), the set xml2rfc's
    templates and kramdown-rfc declare. External and parameter entities,
    any other declaration, and a reference to an entity nobody declared are
    refused.
  - An `include` element (`xi:include`) with a non-empty href is refused:
    nothing is fetched.
  - Input over XML_MAX_INPUT_BYTES, elements nested deeper than
    XML_MAX_DEPTH, an element with more than XML_MAX_ATTRS attributes and
    a DOCTYPE declaring more than XML_MAX_ENTITIES entities are refused
    before they can cost anything. Entities are looked up in a Map, and a
    text node's pieces are joined once, so reading costs the input's
    length.
  - The input must be UTF-8, and a character XML does not allow (U+0000 to
    U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E to U+001F, U+FFFE, U+FFFF) is refused
    wherever it stands, raw or as a character reference.

Every refusal is an XmlError with its XML line and column and, after a
`<?line N?>`, its markdown line. Nothing here panics.

Lines. A `<?line N?>` processing instruction (kramdown-rfc writes one at
the start of the abstract and of each `--- middle` / `--- back` part) says
that the XML line it stands on is markdown line N. Each node and refusal
carries the last such mark before it: its N (`mdLine`) and the XML line it
stands on (`markLine`). The markdown line is known exactly only on the
mark's own line; below it, kramdown-rfc's XML no longer follows the
markdown line for line (a table, a list or a heading takes a different
number of lines in each), so nothing is extrapolated. A signed
`<?line -N?>` or `<?line +N?>` is, as in kramdown-rfc, a correction to
every later unsigned N; it moves no line by itself. N has at most 9 digits.

## Declarations

<a id="xml_max_input_bytes"></a>

### XML_MAX_INPUT_BYTES

Larger input is refused before it is read.

```ts
const XML_MAX_INPUT_BYTES: i32 = ...
```

<a id="xml_max_depth"></a>

### XML_MAX_DEPTH

Elements may nest this deep; one more is refused.

```ts
const XML_MAX_DEPTH: i32 = 256
```

<a id="xml_max_attrs"></a>

### XML_MAX_ATTRS

An element may carry this many attributes; one more is refused.

```ts
const XML_MAX_ATTRS: i32 = 64
```

<a id="xml_max_entities"></a>

### XML_MAX_ENTITIES

A DOCTYPE may declare this many entities; one more is refused.

```ts
const XML_MAX_ENTITIES: i32 = 256
```

### XmlNode

An element, or a run of character data (its `name` is "").

```ts
class XmlNode
```

#### new XmlNode

Makes a node.

```ts
new XmlNode(
  name: string,
  line: i32,
  mdLine: i32,
  markLine: i32,
  id: i32,
): XmlNode
```

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>

the element's name, or "" for character data

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="line" type="i32" required>

its XML line

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="mdLine" type="i32" required>

the last mark's markdown line, or -1

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="markLine" type="i32" required>

the XML line of that mark, or 0

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="id" type="i32" required>

its number in the document

</scalar-field>

```ts

```

#### XmlNode.attrValues


#### XmlNode.col

The 1-based column it starts at, on `line`.

```ts

```

#### XmlNode.first

```ts

```

#### XmlNode.id

A number unique in its document, for keying a node in a Map.

```ts
id: i32
```

#### XmlNode.last

The last child; null without one.

```ts
last: XmlNode | null
```

#### XmlNode.line

The 1-based XML line it starts on.

```ts
line: i32
```

#### XmlNode.markLine

The XML line that `<?line N?>` stands on; 0 when none. `mdLine` is this node's own markdown line only when `line` is this one.

```ts
markLine: i32
```

#### XmlNode.mdLine

The markdown line of the last `<?line N?>` at or before it; -1 when none.

```ts
mdLine: i32
```

#### XmlNode.name

The element's name; "" for character data.

```ts
name: string
```

#### XmlNode.next

The next sibling; null for the last.

```ts
next: XmlNode | null
```

#### XmlNode.parent

The enclosing element; null for the root.

```ts
parent: XmlNode | null
```

#### XmlNode.text

Character data's text, references resolved; "" for an element.

```ts
text: string
```

#### XmlNode.verbatim

Whether character data is written in the XML as its text, character for character from `col`, no reference or CDATA section changing it.

```ts
verbatim: boolean
```

### xmlParse

Reads XML into a tree of elements and character data. Line ends are read
as LF (CRLF and a lone CR alike) and a leading byte-order mark is skipped.

```ts
function xmlParse(text: string): Result<XmlNode, XmlError>
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the input

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;XmlNode, XmlError&gt;">

</scalar-field>
